### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, note references) appear in the supplied §10.2 evidence.** There is therefore no missing footnote text to flag and no footnote commentary to unpack. The qualifications that do appear are embedded in narrative and table rows, and are analysed below.

**Qualification 1 — "surplus position of R10 million … recognition … limited due to the application of the asset limitation criteria in IAS 19."**
- The gross surplus is R10m (2025: R32m), but the **recognised net asset is nil** (2025: R13m) because the IAS 19.64 asset ceiling of R10m (2025: R19m) fully offsets the surplus.
- Implication for forecasting: **no balance-sheet pension asset to release into FCFE**; the pension line contributes zero to net asset value. Any future surplus growth is unrecognisable until the ceiling test changes (e.g., via refund/contribution-holiday entitlement). This is a **non-cash, non-forecastable item** — treat pension P&L as a small recurring cost only.

**Qualification 2 — "closed to new members" / "no longer open to new employees" / registered employees fell 14 → 6.**
- Headcount in the fund halved (14 → 6). Combined with the R39m obligation "Transfers out" and R55m plan-asset "Transfers out," this signals a **bulk transfer/settlement event** during FY2026, not organic run-off.
- Implication: the R8m "Settlement costs" in P&L and the R8m "Settlement" in the obligation roll-forward are **one-off, non-recurring**. Do **not** annualise the R9m FY2026 net periodic pension expense; normalise toward the FY2025 R1m run-rate plus modest interest.

**Qualification 3 — "There is no material investment in Telkom shares."**
- Removes any self-investment/treasury-share circularity risk in the plan assets. Neutral for forecasting; confirms plan-asset fair value is independent of Telkom's own share price.

**Qualification 4 — "Funding level per statutory actuarial valuation 100%."**
- Statutory funding is fully covered, so **no deficit-funding cash calls** expected. Consistent with the R0.3m estimated employer contribution for FY2027 — immaterial to cash flow.

**Arithmetic / reconciliation checks (flagged):**
- **Obligation roll-forward (p.111):** 54 + 4 + 1 − 9 + 6 + 8 − 39 = **25** ✓ (ties to closing obligation R25m).
- **Plan-asset roll-forward (p.112):** 86 + 5 − 9 + 8 − 55 = **35** ✓ (ties to closing R35m).
- **Funded status:** 35 − 25 = **10** surplus ✓; less ceiling (10) = **nil** recognised ✓.
- **OCI reconciliation tension (flag):** The OCI components on p.111 sum to −1 + 3 + 11 = **13**, matching the stated "net periodic pension income recognised in OCI" of R13m. However, the **actuarial loss of R6m on the obligation** (p.111 roll-forward) and the **R8m actuarial gain on plan assets** (p.112) net to a **R2m gain**, which does not obviously bridge to the R13m OCI figure without the R11m asset-ceiling movement. The R11m ceiling movement (2025: −R4m) is the dominant OCI driver and is **not separately explained** — see new question below.
- **Interest cost inconsistency (flag):** P&L "Interest cost on PBO" = R2m (p.111), but the obligation roll-forward shows "Interest cost" = **R4m** (p.111). The R2m difference is unexplained (possibly capitalised or netted against interest on plan assets). **Verification question raised.**
- **Interest on plan assets inconsistency (flag):** P&L shows "Interest on plan assets after asset restriction" = R2m, but the plan-asset roll-forward shows "Interest on plan assets" = **R5m** (p.112). The R3m gap (asset-restriction interest) is not transparently bridged. **Verification question raised.**
- **"Actual return on plan assets" = R10m** (interest 5 + actuarial gain 8 = 13, not 10; or 2 + 8 = 10 using restricted interest). The label is ambiguous — appears to use restricted interest (2 + 8 = 10). Minor presentational inconsistency; note for reconciliation.

      112  Telkom Annual Financial Statements 2026 Introduction statements Annual financial statements Annexures
                                                                                  
      Notes to the annual financial statements continued                          
      for the year ended 31 March 2026                                            
                                                                                  
      10. Employee benefits continued                                             
                                                                                  
      10.3 The Telkom Retirement Fund                                             
                                                                                  
      Significant accounting judgement in the settlement of the TRF               
      In the prior year, the TRF met the IAS 19 (Employee Benefits) criteria for a full settlement of the defined benefit plan, following an amendment
      to the TRF rules, which was approved by the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) with effect from 1 July 2024.
      Management considered whether Telkom has eliminated all further obligations for all the benefits provided under the TRF in order to achieve
      full derecognition of the obligation.                                       
      The rules of the TRF were amended to remove the employer's obligation to make special contributions to the TRF as may be necessary to
      eliminate any actuarial shortfalls in the pensions account by limiting the pensioner liability in the TRF to the balance in the pensions account.
      The amendment of the TRF rules has resulted in Telkom having no further obligation to fund any deficit unless it freely enters into a future
      agreement in writing, creating a future obligation. The views stipulated above were supported by both the pension fund specialist legal counsel
      and actuarial specialists.                                                  
                                                                                  
      Settlement of the TRF                                                       
      The TRF was a hybrid fund which was established on 1 July 1995. The TRF was a defined contribution plan in respect of in-service members
      and a defined benefit plan in respect of pensioners, i.e. members' benefits accrue on a defined contribution basis until retirement. At
      retirement, members have the option to purchase a guaranteed pension from the TRF, at which point they become defined benefit pensioners.
      Prior to 1 July 2024, the option to purchase a pension from the fund was limited to those who joined employment before 1 September 2009,
      but a rule amendment in the TRF extended this benefit option to all retiring employees.
      A rule amendment was registered by the FSCA with effect from 1 July 2024 to remove the employer's obligations to make special contributions
      to the TRF as may be necessary to eliminate any actuarial shortfalls in the pensions account by limiting the pensioner liability in the TRF to the
      balance in the pensions account.                                            
      As a result of the rule amendment, no obligation exists in any scenario for Telkom to make contributions or any other payments to fund any
      deficit in the fund as pension increase percentages and pensions itself may be adjusted to eliminate any shortfall. The rule amendment
      prescribes an investment strategy which mitigates against future deficits. Thus, the amounts available for in-fund pensions will always be equal
      to the amount available in the pensions account. Due to this matching, Telkom will never have any obligation towards the TRF. Therefore,
      Telkom settled the TRF liability as it had no further obligation for part or all of the benefits provided under a defined benefit plan.
      Linked to the rule amendment was an in-principle decision made by the Telkom Board to pay a once-off amount to strengthen the pensioner
      reserves following the rule amendment. This resulted in Telkom having to pay the TRF the once-off amount on approval of the rule amendment
      by the FSCA. In prior year (November 2024), the once-off amount of R330 million was paid to the TRF, funded through the post-retirement
      medical aid (refer to note 10.4) to settle the provision raised in September 2024.
      The gain or loss on settlement was determined as the difference between:    
      – The present value of the defined benefit obligation being settled, as determined on the date of settlement; and
      – The settlement price, including any plan assets transferred and any payments made directly by the entity in connection with the settlement.
       In Telkom's case, the R330 million will form part of the amount that the entity pays in connection with the settlement.
      The amendment changed the nature of the liabilities relating to the fund from a defined benefit to a defined contribution plan (as no further
      Company obligation remains) according to IAS 19, with effect from 1 July 2024.

10.4  Medical benefits
Telkom makes certain contributions to medical aid funds in respect of current and retired employees. The scheme is a defined benefit plan.
The expense in respect of current employees' medical aid is disclosed in note 3.4.3. The amounts due in respect of post-retirement medical
benefits to current and retired employees have been actuarially determined and provided for as set out in note 6.5. Telkom has terminated
future post-retirement medical benefits in respect of employees joining after 1 July 2000.
There are three major categories of members entitled to the post-retirement medical aid: pensioners who retired before 1994 (Pre-94); those
who retired after 2013; and the in-service members. The pensioners retiring post 2013 and the in-service members' liabilities are subject to a
rand cap, which increases as per the Board's approval.
Eligible employees must remain employed by Telkom until retirement age to qualify for the post-retirement medical aid benefit. The most
recent actuarial valuation of the benefit was performed as at 31 March 2026.
The medical aid plan exposes the Group to actuarial risks, such as longevity, currency, interest rate and market risks.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, note refs) are present in the supplied §10.4 evidence.** There is therefore no missing-footnote-text flag to raise for this section. However, several **small-print qualifications and arithmetic tensions** warrant scrutiny:

1. **"The scheme is a defined benefit plan"** — stated for the *medical aid* scheme, yet the roll-forward shows a **fund surplus of R1,017m** and an **asset on the SoFP**. This is unusual: a post-retirement medical plan in *surplus* implies over-funding relative to the actuarial obligation. The **rand cap** qualification ("liabilities subject to a rand cap, which increases as per the Board's approval") is the key driver — the cap limits the company's obligation, which mechanically inflates the apparent surplus. **Verification needed:** the rand cap level, escalation basis, and whether the surplus is recognisable (IAS 19 asset ceiling) or could be reversed.

2. **Reconciliation gap — obligation vs plan assets:**
   - Obligation movement: 1,306 + 116 + 3 + 82 − 181 = **1,326** ✓ (reconciles).
   - Plan assets movement: 2,286 + 212 − 180 + 0 + 25 = **2,343** ✓ (reconciles).
   - **But:** "Benefits paid from plan assets" is **R181m** in the obligation roll-forward vs **R180m** in the plan-asset roll-forward (Group). A **R1m mismatch** — immaterial but should be confirmed as rounding vs a genuine timing difference.
   - **Company column anomaly:** Company obligation opening 1,284, benefits paid **(159)**, closing **1,326**. Check: 1,284 + 116 + 3 + 82 − 159 = **1,326** ✓. But Company plan assets benefits paid = **(180)**, not (159). So Company obligation is reduced by R159m while Company plan assets pay out R180m — a **R21m asymmetry** between the Company obligation and Company plan-asset benefit lines. This is a **reconciliation discrepancy** requiring verification (likely a Group-vs-Company subsidiary allocation, but must be confirmed).

3. **"Employer withdrawal — (332)" in FY2025 plan assets** — a R332m withdrawal from plan assets in the prior year. This is a **cash extraction from the medical plan surplus** and is a material prior-year item. It ties conceptually to the TRF settlement narrative (Q-EB18–Q-EB22 territory) but is **not explained in §10.4**. **Verification needed:** was this withdrawal used to fund the TRF settlement / once-off payment? If so, it links §10.3 and §10.4 cash flows.

4. **Actuarial loss R82m (obligation) vs net OCI expense (57)** — the OCI components sum to −36 + 20 − 41 = **−57**, but the obligation roll-forward shows an **actuarial loss of +82** (increasing obligation). The difference (82 vs 57) is the **plan-asset actuarial gain of +25** (82 − 25 = 57). This reconciles, but confirms the OCI line is **net of asset returns** — a forecast trap if modelling gross obligation vs asset returns separately.

5. **"All equity securities and government bonds have quoted prices in active markets"** — Level 1 fair value hierarchy confirmed for R1,189m equity + R1,062m bonds = **R2,251m of R2,343m (96%)**. Only R39m foreign investments + R53m cash are non-Level-1. Low valuation risk, but **market risk is high**: equity is 51% of plan assets, so a market drawdown directly hits the surplus and OCI.

5. **"Telkom has terminated future post-retirement medical benefits in respect of employees joining after 1 July 2000"** — a **closed-book, run-off plan**. This is a critical forecast driver: the obligation should **decline over time** as pre-2000 cohorts attrite, absent assumption changes. Yet the obligation *rose* from 1,262→1,306→1,326 — driven by interest cost and actuarial losses exceeding benefits paid. **Verification needed:** the actuarial assumption on discount rate and medical inflation, since these drive the direction of the obligation.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`) are present** in the supplied §10.6 table. There is therefore **no missing footnote text to flag** for this section — but note the table carries **no narrative qualification** explaining the base assumptions (discount rate, inflation assumption, mortality basis) against which these sensitivities are struck. - **Asymmetry check (arithmetic tension):** For medical, +0.5% discount = −R38m but −0.5% = +R40m (asymmetric, expected for convexity — acceptable). For telephone rebates, +0.5% = −R13m vs −0.5% = +R14m (mild asymmetry — acceptable). **However**, the telephone rebate **inflation sensitivity is one-sided only** ("Increase in inflation rate to 5%") with **no matching decrease scenario** — unlike medical which shows both ±1%. This is a disclosure gap: the downside (deflation/lower CPI) is not quantified. Flag as Q-TEL8.
- **"Inflation to 5%" is a level, not a delta.** Medical uses "±1%"; telephone rebates use "to 5%". These are **not comparable bases** — the telephone rebate base inflation assumption is undisclosed, so the +R212m cannot be normalised to a per-1% sensitivity without the base rate. Flag Q-TEL9.
- **Retirement-age sensitivity swing:** 58→60 = −R9m (FY26) vs −R22m (FY25); 58→50 = +R33m (FY26) vs +R16m (FY25). The **directionally consistent but magnitude-unstable** pattern (FY25 vs FY26) suggests assumption or membership changes between years — worth reconciling to the pensioner count decline (−14.2% to 11,772 per §10.5). Flag Q-TEL10.
- **Group = Company for every line.** All sensitivities are identical Group vs Company, consistent with the plans sitting in the operating entity — no consolidation adjustment. No issue, but confirms single-entity exposure.
- **Pension (TPF) sensitivities are near-nil (±R1–2m)** — consistent with a **defined-contribution-like or fully-funded** posture; the material unfunded risk sits in **medical and telephone rebates**, not TPF. This reframes forecast risk concentration (see §5).

10.7  Telkom Group employee share scheme
Summary of material accounting policies
The Group has a share-based payment compensation plan. The plan is an equity-settled plan, consisting of the long-term incentive plan (LTIP),
the employee share ownership plan (ESOP) and an additional share award (ASA).
The expense relating to the services rendered by the employees, and the corresponding increase in equity, is measured at the fair value of the
equity instruments at their grant date based on the market price at that date. This compensation cost is recognised over the vesting period,
based on the best available estimate at each reporting date of the number of equity instruments that are expected to vest.
During the vesting period, participants have all the shareholders' rights, including the right to vote and share in any dividend distribution.
Telkom's shareholders approved the Telkom forfeitable share plan (FSP) and the ASA at the September 2013 AGM.
In the FSP, employees acquire shareholder rights on the grant date for the forfeitable shares (these include dividends and voting rights).
An employee turnover assumption of 3.1% to 7.0% has been used in calculating the expected number of shares that will vest. The turnover
relates to the various entities within the Group.

In relation to market-related performance criteria, IFRS 2 requires a fair value to be placed on employee share grants/options. Fair value is
measured as the market price of the entity's share grants/options adjusted for the terms and conditions applicable to the grant/option. Since
employee share grants/options are not traded, there is no market price available. For this reason, the fair value of the grants/options must be
determined by using an option pricing model.

Scrutinize key accounting policies, unusual movements, and forward guidance.

### [SECTION READING RESPONSE / DETERMINATION]
### 1. Answers to Stored Questions for This Section

No stored questions from earlier sections relate to the material in §10.7 (employee share schemes). All stored questions are carried forward unchanged into the Updated Open Questions Ledger below.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Footnote [^1] (pp. 120–121) — Grant 13 / BCX Grant 7 / Openserve Grant 3 (FY2026 LTIP):**
- **Grant date:** 1 December 2025. **Shares granted:** 4,425,803 (matches the "Shares granted during the year" line in the movement table on p. 119 — arithmetic reconciles).
- **Vesting date stated in footnote:** 31 March 2029, vesting 100% if performance conditions met and employee still employed.
- **Tension flagged:** The valuation table (p. 120) labels the same grant "Vesting 29 June 2029," while the footnote says "31 March 2029." This is a ~3-month discrepancy in the vesting date that directly affects the IFRS 2 expense amortisation profile (shorter vesting period → higher annual charge). **Verification question raised (Q-SBP1).**
- **Tension flagged:** The footnote describes the grant as "a fixed number of shares to eligible participating employees at the vesting date" — this is fixed-equity classification language, but the valuation table applies an option-pricing model with volatility (44%) and risk-free rate (6.63%). If the award is truly fixed shares, fair value = market price at grant date (R48.85) with no option model needed. The presence of volatility/risk-free inputs implies either (a) a market-related performance condition (TSR) requiring Monte Carlo, or (b) a classification inconsistency. **Verification question raised (Q-SBP2).**
- **Cross-entity duplication:** The identical footnote text and identical 4,425,803 share count appear under Telkom, BCX, and Openserve tables. The movement table on p. 119 shows Group shares granted = 4,425,803 and Company = 3,242,215. The footnote's 4,425,803 appears to be the **Group total**, not entity-specific — yet it is footnoted to three separate entity tables. **Verification question raised (Q-SBP3).**

**Vesting timeline table inconsistencies (pp. 117–119):**
- **Telkom LTIP 2025 & 2026 grants:** Vesting timelines show 100% in FY2029 and FY2030 respectively, but the "Probability of meeting non-market-related criteria" row shows 40% (FY2029) and 70% (FY2030) — these probabilities are placed in the **2029 and 2030 columns**, not aligned to the 100% vesting column in the same row. This is a column-alignment defect in the table. **Verification question raised (Q-SBP4).**
- **Openserve Grant 2025:** Vesting timeline row shows "— — — 100%" with the 100% appearing to sit in the 2028 column, but the probability row shows 40% in the **2029** column. Misalignment again. **Verification question raised (Q-SBP4).**
- **Gyro table (p. 118):** Column headers show only four vesting years (2026–2029) versus five for all other entities (2026–2030). Gyro grant 2023 shows 50%/30%/20% across 2026–2028 — consistent with the narrative "vest between 2026 and 2028." No FY2030 exposure for Gyro. **Baseline captured.**

**Movement table (p. 119) — arithmetic check:**
- Group: 12,118,701 − 580,675 − 5,602,337 + 4,425,803 = **10,361,492** ✓ (reconciles to stated closing balance).
- Company: 7,562,095 − 499,509 − 2,647,545 + 3,242,215 = **7,657,256** ✓ (reconciles).
- **Flag:** Group forfeited shares (5,602,337) are 46% of opening balance — unusually high. Combined with vested shares (580,675), total attrition = 6,183,012 vs 4,425,803 new grants → net dilution negative. **Verification question raised (Q-SBP5)** on the driver of the high forfeiture (turnover assumption 3.1%–7.0% seems inconsistent with 46% forfeiture — likely performance-condition failures or scheme wind-downs).

**Weighted average remaining vesting period:** 1.52 years (FY2026) vs 0.54 years (FY2025) — a 181% increase, driven by the large FY2026 grant with a ~3.3-year vesting horizon. This implies a **step-up in IFRS 2 amortisation charge in FY2027–FY2029**. **Baseline captured; verification question raised (Q-SBP6)** on the actual IFRS 2 expense line (not disclosed in this section).

**Key performance indicators (p. 121):** HEPS, free cash flow, ROIC, social impact, emissions, TSR. The inclusion of **TSR** confirms at least one market-related condition exists → supports use of option-pricing model for at least some grants (partially addresses Q-SBP2, but the FY2026 Grant 13 footnote still describes fixed shares).

**Volatility basis:** five-year average historical Telkom share price volatility. Volatility ranges 35%–53% across grants — high, consistent with Telkom's distressed equity history. **Baseline captured.**

**Missing footnote text check:** All footnote markers ([^1]) in the supplied evidence have corresponding definitions present. No missing footnote text identified in this section.

### 3. New Questions to Check in Future Sections

- **Q-SBP1 [HIGH]:** Reconcile the FY2026 Grant 13 vesting date — footnote says 31 March 2029, valuation table says 29 June 2029. Which governs the IFRS 2 amortisation period? Check §10.7 continuation or the IFRS 2 expense note.
- **Q-SBP2 [HIGH]:** Confirm whether FY2026 Grant 13 (and BCX Grant 7 / Openserve Grant 3) is fixed-equity (fair value = R48.85 grant-date price) or contains a market-related TSR condition requiring the 44% volatility / 6.63% risk-free option model. Check IFRS 2 expense note and Remuneration Report.
- **Q-SBP3 [MED]:** Confirm whether the 4,425,803 shares in footnote [^1] are the Group total (allocated across Telkom, BCX, Openserve) or triple-counted. Reconcile to the movement table's Group vs Company split (4,425,803 vs 3,242,215).
- **Q-SBP4 [MED]:** Confirm correct column alignment of vesting probabilities for Telkom LTIP 2025/2026 and Openserve Grant 2025 (40% and 70% probabilities appear mis-columned). Check prior-year AFS or scheme rules.
- **Q-SBP5 [MED]:** Explain the 5,602,337 Group forfeitures (46% of opening) — performance-condition failures vs turnover vs scheme closures. Check Remuneration Report and HR disclosures.
- **Q-SBP6 [HIGH]:** Obtain the actual IFRS 2 share-based payment expense for FY2026 and FY2025 (income statement / note). The 1.52-year weighted average vesting period implies a multi-year amortisation tail into FY2027–FY2029 — quantify the annual charge.
- **Q-SBP7 [MED]:** Confirm whether the ESOP schemes (Telkom, BCX, Trudon, Gyro, Openserve) are equity-settled or cash-settled, and whether any carry employer tax (PAYE) obligations that create a cash cost separate from the IFRS 2 non-cash charge.
- **Q-SBP8 [LOW]:** Confirm the treatment of dividends paid on unvested forfeitable shares (participants have dividend rights per policy) — are these deducted from the IFRS 2 expense or paid in cash?

**Forecast implications flagged (not narrative — arithmetic only):**
- 1.52-year weighted average vesting period × 10.36m shares × ~R48.85 grant price ≈ **R770m unamortised IFRS 2 pool** (rough order of magnitude; actual depends on grant-by-grant fair values and probabilities). Amortisation tail into FY2027–FY2029 is material to the non-cash expense line and must be sourced from the IFRS 2 note (Q-SBP6).
- Forfeiture rate of 46% (Group) vs turnover assumption of 3.1%–7.0% is a **~7–15× gap** — either performance conditions are failing at scale or the turnover assumption is not the binding constraint. This affects the expected-vesting estimate and therefore the annual IFRS 2 charge (Q-SBP5).

### [SECTION READING RESPONSE / DETERMINATION]
### 1. Answering Stored Questions from Earlier Sections

**Q-SBP3 (share-count allocation) — PARTIALLY ADDRESSED.** The director shareholding table shows direct beneficial holdings of 327,783 shares (executives) and 5,500 (non-executives) at 31 March 2026, versus 268,389 at 31 March 2025. The increase of 59,394 shares (S Taukobong +56,594; M Booi +3,000; B Kennedy −200) is consistent with share-scheme vesting but the table does not reconcile to the §10.7 scheme share pool. **Residual open.**

**Q-SBP7 (settlement/tax treatment) — PARTIALLY ADDRESSED.** The footnote `[^1]` confirms remuneration includes "company contribution to the TRF and flexible benefits" — i.e., the TRF is an employer-funded defined-contribution-style vehicle, not a share-settled scheme. This is consistent with the §10.7 finding that TRF is nil. **Residual open** on whether any share-scheme awards are equity- or cash-settled.

**Q-EQ2 (confirm no other schemes) — PARTIALLY ADDRESSED.** §11.1 evidences only director shareholding and emoluments; no additional share scheme is disclosed here. **Residual open** pending §11.2–§11.5 (related-party transactions, subsidiaries, associates, JVs, key management).

All other stored questions (Q-SBP1, Q-SBP2, Q-SBP4, Q-SBP5, Q-SBP6, Q-SBP8, Q-EB5, Q-EB6, Q-TEL6, Q-TR, Q-DIV7–Q-DIV9, Q-T10, Q-T11, Q-T18, Q-T23, Q-L14, Q-L15, Q-J1, Q-J2, Q-T24, Q-EQ13, Q-T22, Q-MED9–Q-MED13, Q-TEL1, Q-TEL8–Q-TEL10, Q-SENS1, Q-SENS2, and the full carried-forward ledger) are **not addressed by this section** and carry forward unchanged.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Footnote `[^1]` (p.123):** *"Remuneration includes basic salary, company contribution to the TRF and flexible benefits."*
- **Implication:** The TRF (Telkom Retirement Fund) is an employer-contribution vehicle embedded in executive remuneration, not a share-based payment. This is consistent with the §10.7 finding that TRF is nil and with the §10.4 medical scheme disclosure. It does **not** resolve whether any executive awards are settled in shares vs cash — the "Remuneration" column (R17,268,625 for Taukobong; R7,268,625 for Dlamoye) is a single aggregate and does not split salary vs share-based compensation.
- **Verification tension:** The "Performance bonus" column (R10,000,000 for CEO; R5,000,000 for CFO) is disclosed separately, but there is no line for share-based payment expense. If §10.7 share schemes vested in FY2026, the IFRS 2 expense should appear either in remuneration or in the §10.7 note — **Q-SBP6 remains open** and must be reconciled against the §10.7 IFRS 2 expense quantum.

**No footnote markers are missing** in this section — `[^1]` is the only marker and its definition is present.

**Arithmetic checks on supplied numbers:**
- Non-executive total: 8,871,510 + 7,114,134 = **15,985,644** ✓ (matches table).
- Executive total: 17,736,863 + 16,359,756 + 12,588 = **34,109,207** ✓.
- CEO: 10,468,238 + 10,000,000 + 12,292 = **20,480,530** ✓.
- CFO: 7,268,625 + 6,359,756 + 296 = **13,628,677** ✓.
- Grand total: 15,985,644 + 34,109,207 = **50,094,851** ✓.
- **No arithmetic tension detected** in the emoluments table.

**Director shareholding reconciliation:**
- FY2026 executive direct beneficial: 322,283 (Taukobong) + 0 (Dlamini) = **322,283** ✓.
- FY2026 non-executive direct beneficial: 2,500 + 3,000 = **5,500** ✓.
- FY2025 executive: 265,689; FY2025 non-executive: 2,700. **Increase of 56,594 (CEO) and 2,800 (non-exec) — consistent with vesting but not reconciled to §10.7 scheme pool → Q-SBP3 residual.**

**Table structural issue:** The header row shows "Group and Company" repeated and the column alignment for "Beneficial/Non-Beneficial" and "Direct/Indirect" is visually ambiguous in the captured text. **Q-SBP4 (table column misalignment) remains open** — the capture does not definitively confirm whether the 322,283 is direct-beneficial or indirect-beneficial.

### 3. New Questions to Check in Future Sections

- **Q-RP1 [HIGH]:** §11.1 discloses only director shareholding and emoluments. Where are the **related-party transactions** (subsidiaries, associates, JVs, key management compensation, government-related entities — given the Government Employees Pension Fund / PIC shareholding)? Must be checked in §11.2–§11.5 (pp. 123–126).
- **Q-RP2 [HIGH]:** The **"Government-related entities"** exemption (IAS 24.25–27) — does Telkom disclose transactions with the South African government (its largest shareholder via PIC/GEPF) and related entities (Eskom, Transnet, SABC, Sentech, etc.)? Check §11.2–§11.5.
- **Q-RP3 [MED]:** **Key management compensation** — is the R50,094,851 director emolument total the full key-management figure, or is there a separate "key management personnel" disclosure including prescribed officers? Check §11.2–§11.5.
- **Q-RP4 [MED]:** **Associates and JVs** — are there any equity-accounted investees (e.g., BCX, Gyro, Trudon, Yellow Pages) with related-party balances? Check §11.2–§11.5 and the investments note.
- **Q-RP5 [MED]:** **Subsidiary transactions** — intra-group loans, guarantees, and management fees that could affect consolidation and FCFE. Check §11.2–§11.5.
- **Q-RP6 [LOW]:** **Directors' loans / guarantees** — any advances to directors or prescribed officers? Not disclosed in §11.1; check §11.2–§11.5.
- **Q-RP7 [LOW]:** **Post-balance-sheet director changes** — the note states "no change since 31 March 2026 to date of approval"; confirm the approval date and whether any director resigned/appointed after that date. Check the directors' report / subsequent events note.

### [SECTION READING RESPONSE / DETERMINATION]
### 1. Answers to Stored Questions for This Section

**Q-SBP3 residual [MED] — director shareholding increase vs §10.7 scheme pool.**
Partially answered. §11.1 (p.123) shows CEO direct beneficial holding rose from 265,689 (FY2025) to 322,283 (FY2026) = **+56,594 shares**. §11.1 (p.124) footnote states **66,711 shares vested to Mr S Taukobong** in FY2026 (FY2025: 531,699 vested). The +56,594 net increase is *less* than the 66,711 vested — implying ~10,117 shares were disposed/sold (or net-of-tax withholding) post-vesting. This is consistent with a vesting event but the **gross-to-net reconciliation (66,711 vested → 56,594 net holding increase) is not disclosed** and cannot be closed from §11.1 alone. Carry forward as **Q-SBP3 residual** to §10.7 / directors' report.

**Q-SBP7 residual [MED] — equity vs cash settlement of share schemes.**
Partially answered. Footnote `[^1]` (p.123 and p.124) confirms remuneration includes "company contribution to the TRF and flexible benefits" — i.e. TRF is an **employer cash contribution**, not share-settled. However, the IFRS 2 expense (R10,236,291 CEO; R2,702,091 CFO; p.124) is disclosed separately from remuneration, confirming **equity-settled IFRS 2 expense sits outside the emoluments table**. Residual: whether any portion is cash-settled (IFRS 2 liability classification) is not stated → carry forward **Q-SBP7 residual**.

**Q-EQ2 residual [MED] — additional schemes.**
Partially answered. §11.1 discloses only the Telkom share scheme (IFRS 2) for executives; no additional scheme named. Residual pending §11.2–§11.5 (related-party note continuation) and §10.7 → carry forward **Q-EQ2 residual**.

**Q-RP1–Q-RP7 [NEW from §11.1]** — these were raised *by* this section; they cannot be answered here. Carry forward (see §4).

*All other stored questions relate to sections not present in this capture (tax, leases, hedges, medical, etc.) and are carried forward unanswered.*

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Footnote `[^1]` (p.123 & p.124) — "Remuneration includes basic salary, company contribution to the TRF and flexible benefits."**
- Confirms TRF (Telkom Retirement Fund) is an **employer cash contribution embedded in remuneration**, not a separate share-settled item. This closes the *classification* question (Q-SBP7 partial) but the **quantum of the TRF contribution inside remuneration is not separately disclosed** for directors — only for Prescribed Officers (13% column, p.125).
- Implication: director "remuneration" is a **gross cash cost**; no IFRS 2 element is buried in it. The IFRS 2 expense is disclosed separately (p.124) → clean separation for forecasting opex vs non-cash SBP.

**Footnote `[^2]` (p.125) — "Fringe and other benefits include motor car insurance, retention bonus, separation packages and leave payments."**
- **Critical for forecasting**: the FY2026 Prescribed Officer "fringe and other benefits" of **R9,815,025** (vs R8,403,156 FY2025) is inflated by **separation packages** (PJ Bogoshi R3,032,160; LM Siyo R6,343,703; S Mmakau R417,626). These are **non-recurring** — must be stripped from run-rate opex. LM Siyo's R6.34m fringe on a R6.39m remuneration base is almost entirely separation/retention, not recurring.
- **Verification flag**: separation packages are not separately quantified per individual; the split between retention bonus, separation, and leave pay is opaque → new question Q-RP8.

**Footnote `[^3]` (p.125) — "The pension contribution is a company contribution."**
- Confirms the 13% TRF column (R2,482,030 FY2026; R3,245,280 FY2025) is **employer cost, additional to remuneration**. Note the 13% column does **not** reconcile to 13% of remuneration for all officers (e.g. BN Apleni: 13% × R4,500,000 = R585,000 but disclosed R339,300) → contribution base is **pensionable salary, not total remuneration**. Flag as Q-RP9.

**Footnotes `[^4]`–`[^7]` (p.125) — appointments/resignations.**
- BN Apleni appointed Openserve CEO **1 July 2025** (9 months) — remuneration R4.5m is part-year.
- PJ Bogoshi resigned BCX CEO **28 February 2026** (11 months) — R3.03m fringe = separation.
- AC Beukes resigned Openserve CEO **13 December 2024** — FY2025 comparative only.
- DJ Reyneke resigned **31 October 2025** (7 months) — FY2025 comparative.
- **Forecast implication**: FY2026 Prescribed Officer cost (R65.07m) is **not a clean run-rate** — contains part-year appointments, separations, and a CEO transition. FY2027 run-rate should be modelled off **full-year incumbent remuneration** (Apleni full-year, Bogoshi replaced, Siyo separation removed).

**Arithmetic checks performed:**
- Non-exec emoluments FY2026: sum of individual totals = R15,985,644 ✓ (ties to subtotal).
- Executive emoluments FY2026: 20,480,530 + 13,628,677 = **R34,109,207** ✓.
- Total emoluments paid by Telkom FY2026: 15,985,644 + 34,109,207 = **R50,094,851** ✓.
- Prescribed Officers FY2026: sum of six totals = 10,149,234 + 8,711,029 + 9,196,845 + 8,516,335 + 9,123,630 + 19,368,025 = **R65,065,098** ✓.
- **Discrepancy flagged**: Prescribed Officer remuneration column sums to R30,489,607 and incentive bonus to R24,760,466; 30,489,607 + 24,760,466 + 9,815,025 = **R65,065,098** ✓ — reconciles.
- **Tension flagged**: LM Siyo total R19,368,025 is an outlier (fringe R6,343,703) — separation package inflates; not a run-rate. → Q-RP8.

**Missing footnote text check:** All footnote markers in the supplied evidence (`[^1]`–`[^7]`) have definitions present. **No missing footnote text in this capture.** However, the **directors' report cross-reference** ("Refer to the Directors report for appointments and resignations") is not in this capture → Q-RP10.

11.2  Related party transactions and balances
The South African Government, represented by the Department of Communication and Digital Technologies, exercises significant influence over
the Group. Telkom is classified as a Schedule 2 major public entity in terms of the Public Finance Management Act. Telkom is part of the
national sphere of government, and its related parties in that sphere include national departments, constitutional institutions and public entities
(schedule 1, 2 and 3). Telkom is therefore related to major public entities, national government departments and all other entities within the
national sphere of government. A list of related parties is provided by National Treasury on its website (www.treasury.gov.za).
Related parties include subsidiaries and associates of the Group. It also includes Directors and key management personnel of Telkom and close
family members of these related parties. Key management personnel and Directors for Telkom include the Group’s Board of Directors and Exco.
The Group has applied the exemption in IAS 24 paragraph 25 in respect of related party transactions and outstanding balances with
government-related entities. The nature of the Group's transactions with these entities are within the ordinary course of operations.
At 31 March 2026, the Government of South Africa held 40.5% (31 March 2025: 40.5%) of Telkom's shares and had the ability to exercise
significant influence, and the Public Investment Corporation held 11.08% (31 March 2025: 8.44%) of Telkom's shares.

Refer to notes 12.2 and 12.3 for details."* → Confirms Swiftnet is a **discontinued/divested** related party; FY2026 column is Rnil across all lines (expenses, dividend received, interest received/expense). **Verification implication:** the FY2025 comparative (expenses R339m, dividend received R365m, interest received R35m, interest expense R1m) must be excluded from FY2027 forecast run-rate. - `[^2]` Acajou Investments t/a VS Gaming — *"Deregistered in the current year."* → FY2026 balances Rnil; FY2025 shows offsetting other receivables (R92m) and trade payables R92m (sign presentation inconsistent — receivable shown as negative). **Verification implication:** confirm no residual liability/asset survives deregistration; confirm any derecognition gain/loss.
- `[^3]` Gyro Group (Pty) Ltd — *"Divisionalised in the current year."* → FY2026 balances largely unwound (trade receivables Rnil vs R8m; other receivables Rnil vs R38m; trade payables R5m vs (R116)m). **Verification implication:** "divisionalised" implies Gyro Group ceased to be a separate legal related party and was absorbed into a division — confirm whether intercompany balances were eliminated on divisionalisation and whether the R5m payable is a residual.

**Footnote markers with MISSING definitions — flag explicitly:**
- **p.127: No footnote markers present** on the Company subsidiary table (Business Connexion, Openserve, Trudon, Swiftnet, Acajou, Telkom Foundation, Rossal No 65). No missing-definition issue on this page.
- **p.126: No footnote markers** on the Prescribed Officer tables. No missing-definition issue.
- **p.128: All three markers (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, `[^3]`) have definitions supplied.** No missing footnote text identified in this capture.

**Qualification / commentary unpacking (p.126, §11.2 narrative):**
- **IAS 24 para 25 exemption applied** for government-related entities: *"The Group has applied the exemption in IAS 24 paragraph 25 in respect of related party transactions and outstanding balances with government-related entities. The nature of the Group's transactions with these entities are within the ordinary course of operations."* → **Forecast implication:** material revenue from government/SOC customers (e.g., SITA, SAPO, national departments) is **NOT separately quantified** in this note. This is a disclosure gap — government revenue concentration cannot be verified from §11.2 alone. Must be cross-checked against segment revenue note and credit-risk note.
- **Shareholding:** Government 40.5% (unchanged YoY); **PIC 11.08% (FY2025: 8.44%)** → PIC increased stake by **+2.64pp**. Verification implication: confirm whether PIC accumulation is market purchase or block trade; relevant to free-float and potential overhang.
- **Schedule 2 major public entity / PFMA** classification — confirms government-related-party perimeter is broad (all national departments, schedule 1/2/3 entities). Forecast implication: procurement/transparency constraints and potential MTR/regulatory interplay.

**Arithmetic checks on supplied numbers:**
- **Prescribed Officer IFRS 2 total FY2026:** 2,529,756 + 4,449,648 + 1,182,503 + 1,251,154 + 6,331,526 = **15,744,587** ✓ ties to stated total.
- **Prescribed Officer IFRS 2 total FY2025:** 1,937,277 + 3,267,580 + 2,234,598 + 580,787 + 617,086 + 2,194,743 + 2,908,063 = **13,740,134** ✓ ties to stated total.
- **Vested shares FY2026 total:** 12,062 + 290,648 + 0 + 0 + 344,712 = **647,422** ✓ ties.
- **Vested shares FY2025 total:** 365,884 + 425,139 + 278,070 + 0 + 0 + 259,282 + 316,489 = **1,644,864** ✓ ties.
- **Key management compensation (Group FY2026):** 325 + 15 + 12 + 35 = **387** (not stated as total; components only). FY2025: 270 + 15 + 9 + 21 = **315**. Company FY2026: 256 + 12 + 7 + 31 = **306**; FY2025: 208 + 11 + 7 + 24 = **250**. No stated total to reconcile against — flag as minor.
- **Openserve interest received R817m vs loan receivable R8,767m** → implied yield ≈ **9.3%**; FY2025 R903m / R8,743m ≈ **10.3%**. Yield compression of ~100bp — **flag** (Q-RP15).
- **Openserve expenses R5,277m vs revenue R998m** — Company-level intercompany cost is large; consistent with Openserve as wholesale infrastructure provider to Telkom. No arithmetic tension, but note the asymmetry.

**Sign/presentation anomalies to flag:**
- Acajou FY2025: other receivables **(92)** and trade payables **92** — receivable shown negative. Presentation inconsistency (Q-RP16).
- Gyro Group FY2026 trade payables **5** (positive) vs FY2025 **(116)** — sign flip; confirm whether R5m is a payable or a net debit (Q-RP17).
- Business Connexion "Revenue and other income **(789)**" and "Dividend received **(490)**" shown in brackets (credit) — consistent with income presentation, but confirm these are eliminations at Company level, not Group revenue.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Footnote definitions present in this section:** `[^1]`, `[^2]`, `[^3]` (first table) and `[^1]`, `[^2]` (second table). **No missing footnote text** — all markers have supplied definitions.

**`[^1]` (first table) — Acajou Investments t/a VS Gaming:** *"Deregistration was finalised in the current year."* Implication: VS Gaming (100% held, issued share capital Rnil FY2026 vs R100 FY2025) has been **deregistered**. This is a group-composition change — confirm whether any residual assets/liabilities, tax deregistration costs, or disposal gain/loss flowed through FY2026 P&L, and whether VS Gaming revenue/EBITDA (not separately disclosed) was previously consolidated and now ceases. **Verification question raised (Q-GC1).**

**`[^2]` (first table) — Number Portability Company:** *"There are no significant restrictions on the ability of the associate to transfer funds to the Group in the form of cash dividends, or to repay loans or advances made by the Group."* Implication: NPC (20%, equity-accounted, carrying value R13m) is **repatriation-clean**. Immaterial to group cash, but confirms no FX/central-bank lock at this associate. No forecast impact beyond confirming associate dividend capacity is unconstrained.

**`[^3]` (first table) — Gyro Group (Pty) Ltd:** *"Gyro Group was divisionalised into Telkom Company in the current financial year."* Implication: Gyro Group (100%, issued capital Rnil FY2026 vs R100 FY2025) has been **absorbed into Telkom Company (the holding operating company)**. This is an internal reorganisation — confirm no gain/loss, no change in tax residence, and that Gyro Group's FY2026 stub results (revenue Rnil, EBIT (18), net loss (18)) reflect only the pre-divisionalisation period. **Verification question raised (Q-GC2).**

**`[^1]` (second table) — Telkom Foundation:** *"Non-profit making trust."* Implication: Telkom Foundation is consolidated (revenue R71m FY2026, EBITDA (2), net loss (1)) despite being a non-profit trust — confirm consolidation basis (control vs significant influence) and whether Foundation spend is a deductible CSI/ED expense or a non-deductible donation for tax-cash forecasting. **Verification question raised (Q-GC3).**

**`[^2]` (second table) — Swiftnet SOC Ltd:** *"In the prior year, Telkom sold its 100% shareholding in Swiftnet effective 31 January 2025. The above interest in operating profits, before eliminations, is for a period of 10 months up until 31 January 2025. Refer to note 12.2."* Implication: **Swiftnet (tower company) was disposed of effective 31 Jan 2025** — FY2025 comparatives include 10 months of Swiftnet (revenue R1,221m, EBITDA R912m, EBIT R819m, net profit R576m). This is a **major forecast base-effect**: FY2026 has **zero** Swiftnet contribution, so group revenue/EBITDA YoY is structurally depressed by the disposal. Critically, this also means **tower lease costs previously internal to Swiftnet may now be external lease payments to the acquirer (IFRS 16 lease liabilities)** — confirm in §12.2 and lease notes. **Verification questions raised (Q-GC4, Q-GC5).**

**Arithmetic checks on supplied numbers:**
- **Openserve FY2026:** Revenue 12,632; EBITDA 4,219 → EBITDA margin = 4,219/12,632 = **33.4%**. FY2025: 4,005/12,349 = **32.4%**. Margin expansion +1.0pp — plausible, no tension.
- **BCX FY2026:** Revenue 11,412; EBITDA 1,104 → margin **9.7%**. FY2025: 1,189/12,345 = **9.6%**. Flat — no tension.
- **Openserve EBIT vs EBITDA FY2026:** EBITDA 4,219 − EBIT 1,863 = **D&A 2,356**. FY2025: 4,005 − 1,525 = **D&A 2,480**. D&A fell R124m YoY despite capex — flag as **Q-GC6** (possible asset disposal/impairment or shorter-lived asset base).
- **Gyro Properties FY2026:** Revenue 1; EBITDA 92; EBIT 91; net profit 103. Net profit > EBIT by R12m — implies **net finance income or tax credit** of ~R12m. Flag as **Q-GC7** (unusual — property company with R1m revenue but R92m EBITDA suggests intercompany rental/management fees; confirm elimination on consolidation).
- **Gyro Group FY2026:** Revenue Rnil; EBITDA (18); EBIT (24); net loss (18). EBIT more negative than EBITDA by R6m (D&A R6m on nil revenue) — consistent with a dormant/divisionalised entity. No tension.
- **Telkom Foundation FY2026:** Revenue 71; EBITDA (2); EBIT (2); net loss (1). Net loss < EBIT by R1m (tax credit or finance income). Minor — no flag.
- **Non-controlling interest:** Text states total NCI R15m FY2026 (R16m FY2025) relating to BCX and Trudon. But table shows BCX and Trudon as **100% owned with NCI "—"**. **Reconciliation tension:** if BCX and Trudon are 100% owned, where does R15m NCI arise? Flag as **Q-GC8** (possible sub-subsidiary NCI below BCX/Trudon, or text/table inconsistency).
- **Number Portability Company carrying value:** R13m FY2026 vs R12m FY2025 — +R1m equity-accounted movement. Immaterial.

### [SECTION READING RESPONSE / DETERMINATION]
### 1. Answers to Stored Questions for This Section

**Q-GC1 — VS Gaming (Acajou Investments) deregistration: was the entity loss-making at derecognition, and what was the P&L/OCI impact?**
Partially answered. `[^1]` confirms "Deregistration was finalised in the current year." The entity carries Rnil issued share capital and Rnil ownership at 31 March 2026 (vs R100 / 100% at 31 March 2025), and is absent from the FY2026 operating-profit table. **Residual open:** the derecognition gain/loss, cash distributed on winding-up, and whether any residual liability (e.g. gaming licence obligations) transferred to Telkom SA SOC are not disclosed here → carried as **Q-GC11**.

**Q-GC2 — Number Portability Company associate: is the 20% interest equity-accounted, and are there transfer restrictions?**
Answered. `[^2]` states: "There are no significant restrictions on the ability of the associate to transfer funds to the Group in the form of cash dividends, or to repay loans or advances made by the Group." Carrying value R13m (FY2025: R12m) — a R1m equity-accounted movement. This **closes the NPC repatriation leg of Q-D9/GG4/HH4/II4/AAA16**; subsidiary-level and cross-border legs remain open (Q-GC10).

**Q-GC3 — Gyro Group divisionalisation: what is the accounting treatment and any gain/loss?**
Partially answered. `[^3]` confirms "Gyro Group was divisionalised into Telkom Company in the current financial year." Table shows Gyro Group FY2026 revenue Rnil, EBITDA (R18)m, EBIT (R24)m, net loss (R18)m — i.e. residual costs only, no revenue, consistent with a post-divisionalisation shell. **Residual open:** whether the divisionalisation was a common-control transaction at carrying value (no gain) and where the FY2025 Gyro Group revenue of R161m / EBITDA (R12)m now sits within Telkom Company segment → **Q-GC12**.

**Q-GC4 — Swiftnet disposal: is the 10-month stub period correctly excluded from FY2026 comparatives?**

The above interest in operating profits, before eliminations, is for a period of 10 months up until 31 January 2025." **Footnote `[^1]` (discontinued operation, p.131):** *"Presented net of intercompany transactions between Swiftnet and other Telkom Group entities."*

For forecasting, the **R4,408m gain is the dominant, non-recurring item**; the underlying operating EBITDA of Swiftnet (pre-gain) is only **R517m** (R4,925m − R4,408m). No footnote explains the composition. → **New Q-G33** (capex vs disposal proceeds split within investing).
